info.title: Ampost API
info.description: Publish to Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn (coming soon), TikTok (coming soon), Threads, X, YouTube, Pinterest, Bluesky, Telegram, Discord with one API. LinkedIn and TikTok are coming soon. A coming-soon platform is listed with `availability: "coming_soon"` in GET /api/platforms and answers 403 `PLATFORM_COMING_SOON` until it opens to your account. Every operation is also an MCP tool at /mcp with the same input and output.

get.description:
List every supported platform with its rules: text length, link support, scheduling, unpublish (delete a published post), editPublished (edit a published post's text), firstComment (comment posted after publish, and its length), thread (follow-up posts, and how many), media types, counts, sizes and required metadata, placements by media shape, and the JSON Schema of its `options`. `availability` is `coming_soon` for a platform that is listed but not open to every account yet: for those accounts, connecting it, posting to it and reading its posts or analytics return 403 PLATFORM_COMING_SOON. Read this instead of hardcoding platform differences, and check a post against these rules and its accounts with posts_validate before posts_create.

MCP tool: `platforms_list`. Key scope: `posts:read`.

get.description:
List your posts, newest created first, as full post objects (status, text, media, schedule, targets and `platformPosts`, the result per account). Use it to find posts: filter by `status`, `platform`, `platformSetId` (posts with an account in that set) or `search` (text match); filters combine. To read one post whose id you have, use posts_get; for views, likes and other metrics, use analytics_posts. Paginated with `limit` and `offset`; `pagination.hasMore` says whether another page exists. A key restricted to some platform sets sees only their posts. An unknown `platformSetId` is 404 PLATFORM_SET_NOT_FOUND.

MCP tool: `posts_list`. Key scope: `posts:read`.

post.summary: Create, schedule or publish a post
post.description:
Create a post for one or more platforms. `targets` lists platform sets, each with its platforms; omit `platformSetId` for your default set. List several sets to reach several accounts of the same platform in one post (each set holds one account per platform); `platformPosts` then has one entry per account. Without `scheduledFor` it is a draft; set `publishNow` to publish it right away, or `scheduledFor` to publish later. `media` items are public URLs with a required `type` (REST also accepts multipart file uploads up to 4 MB per request; for larger files or files on the user's device use media_upload_create). Use `options.<platform>` for per-platform text and settings. `firstComment` is posted as a comment (a reply on X, Threads and Bluesky) on each new post right after it publishes; a failed comment leaves the post published with `platformPosts[].firstComment.status` failed. `thread` adds follow-up posts on X, Bluesky and Threads, each a reply to the one before (results in `platformPosts[].thread`). Call platforms_list (GET /api/platforms) for each platform's limits, placements and options.

MCP tool: `posts_create`. Key scope: `posts:write`.

post.summary: Check a post without creating it
post.description:
Check a posts_create request without creating, counting or publishing anything: same input, same checks and error codes. `valid` is true when posts_create would accept it and, with `publishNow`, every account would publish. `errors` holds the post's own problems (content, schedule, plan features, the 30-day post quota, for publishNow the hourly publish limit); `targets` has one entry per platform of each target with its own `valid`, `errors` (platform set, the platform's rules for text, media, placement and options, a Pinterest `boardId` the account cannot pin to, the account it publishes through, its health, and for publishNow the per-account quota), `warnings` (`ALT_TEXT_NOT_SENT` for alt text the platform leaves out, `BOARD_NOT_CHECKED` when Pinterest did not answer the `options.pinterest.boardId` check, account issues to fix before a scheduled post publishes, a login that expires soon; account health issues carry the `accounts_get` health codes) and `mediaConversion` (what Ampost would convert on that platform, per media item). Each platform reports its first rule error, like posts_create. A request that does not fit the schema answers 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` like posts_create. Takes no post quota, publish limit or X units.

MCP tool: `posts_validate`. Key scope: `posts:read`.

post.description:
Create many posts from a CSV file: one post per row, each checked like posts_create. Columns: `text`, `platforms` (space-separated, with an optional `platformSetId`) or `accountIds`, `scheduledFor` or `useQueue` (neither: a draft), `linkUrl`, `media` (space-separated public URLs; `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.mov` and `.webm` are videos, the rest images) and `text_<platform>` for per-platform text. The dashboard's CSV export has the same columns, so an exported file imports again (its read-only columns are skipped). Send `dryRun: true` first: it checks every row without creating anything. A bad row does not stop the others; `rows[]` gives each row's `status` (`valid`, `created` or `error`) and `errors` with the column. Unknown columns are skipped with a warning. Plans import at most 50 (Free), 1,000 (Pro), 2,500 (Max) or 5,000 (Scale) rows per request. An import and a dry run each take one token per row from the hourly `importPosts` limit (two runs of the plan's largest file an hour, e.g. a dry run and its import); a file with more rows than are left fails with 429 `RATE_LIMITED` and creates nothing. Send an idempotency key with the import: a retry with the same key and file returns the first result and creates nothing new. REST also accepts multipart with the file in a part named `file`.

MCP tool: `posts_import_csv`. Key scope: `posts:write`.

Each account's result is in `platformPosts`: an edited account's `text` holds the new text, and an account the platform refused keeps its text with `notice` (`EDIT_NOT_SUPPORTED` on Instagram, Threads, TikTok, Bluesky and X, and on Facebook stories; the platform's own refusal otherwise). Facebook edits only posts Ampost published; a Telegram caption under media stays limited to 1024 characters. YouTube and Pinterest replace the video or Pin description. YouTube edits and deletes share a budget of 10 a day per channel (3 on Free); past it the account gets `notice` `RATE_LIMITED`. Call platforms_list for `editPublished.supported` per platform. To change a draft or scheduled post, use posts_update. 404 POST_NOT_FOUND for an id that is not yours; 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION when no given account has it published.

MCP tool: `posts_edit_published`. Key scope: `posts:write`.

post.description:
Publish again to the accounts that failed, or only to the given `accountIds` (from `platformPosts[].accountId`). Ampost already retries retryable failures (rate limits, timeouts, platform errors) by itself, up to 5 attempts with backoff; an account waiting for that shows `pending` with `nextAttemptAt`. Call this for an account that is `failed`, after fixing the cause. It starts `attempts` again from 0. A published account whose first comment failed (`platformPosts[].firstComment.status` failed) posts only the comment again, without publishing the post twice or counting it again. An account whose thread stopped at a failed item continues the thread from that item, without publishing the post or the earlier items again. To publish a draft or scheduled post, use posts_publish. 404 POST_NOT_FOUND for an id that is not yours; 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION unless the post is `partial` or `failed` (or only first comments failed).

MCP tool: `posts_retry`. Key scope: `posts:write`.

get.description:
List your social accounts, optionally only one platform or one platform set. `status` defaults to `active`, the accounts that can publish; pass `revoked` for disconnected accounts or `all` for both. Fix with accounts_connect and the account's id as `accountId`. `platformMetadata` has public per-platform details, such as the TikTok creator's allowed privacy levels. Use it to see what a user can post to or to find an account id; use accounts_get to re-check one account whose id you have, and platform_sets_list for the sets themselves. Paginated with `limit` and `offset`. A key restricted to some sets sees only their accounts; an unknown `platformSetId` is 404 PLATFORM_SET_NOT_FOUND.

post.description:
Create a short-lived Ampost-hosted link that connects one social account to a platform set. The user opens `connectUrl` in a browser and authorizes there; consent cannot happen in chat. In MCP, a client that supports URL elicitation asks the user to open the page itself, and the result then has no `connectUrl`. For a new connection, `expectedUsername` or `expectedPlatformAccountId` makes sure the user signs in to the right account. If the user signs in to another account, the request fails with ACCOUNT_MISMATCH and nothing changes. A new request replaces the pending one for the same platform and set, also one the user opened but did not finish (it fails with SUPERSEDED), so call this again when the user lost or closed the page. A coming-soon platform (`availability: coming_soon` in platforms_list) returns 403 PLATFORM_COMING_SOON for accounts it is not open to yet, reconnects included.

Pass `postId` for one post. `analyticsStatus` says why an entry has no metrics. post.description:
Send events to an https URL. Ampost POSTs each event as JSON, signed with the webhook's secret (`Ampost-Signature`), and retries a failed delivery 7 times (1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h and 24 h). After 5 deliveries in a row fail all retries the webhook is turned off. At most 10 webhooks. The response is the only one with the full `secret`: store it now. Revoking the key or app that created the webhook turns it off. Events: post.scheduled, post.unscheduled, post.discarded, post.published, post.partial, post.failed, post.platform.published, post.platform.failed, post.platform.deleted, post.platform.edited, account.connected, account.disconnected, account.needs_reconnect, analytics.synced. Webhooks see every platform set, so keys restricted to some sets get 403 PLATFORM_SET_NOT_ALLOWED.

MCP tool: `webhooks_create`. Key scope: `webhooks:write`.

apiKey.description:
An Ampost API key from Setup → API keys. Each operation needs one scope (its `security` entry); a key without it gets 403 `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`.
A key restricted to platform sets sees only those sets; writes to other sets get 403 `PLATFORM_SET_NOT_ALLOWED`. Scopes:
- `posts:read`: List and read posts and posting queues, and read platform rules
- `posts:write`: Create, change, publish, retry, delete and import posts; edit posting queues
- `accounts:read`: List and read accounts, platform sets and connection requests
- `accounts:write`: Connect and disconnect accounts; create, rename and delete platform sets
- `media:write`: Upload media for posts and check an upload's status. There is no read scope: only the key that uploads needs the status
- `analytics:read`: Read post metrics, account overviews and follower history
- `webhooks:write`: List, read, create, change, test and delete webhooks, read their delivery logs, and redeliver events. Reading needs it too: webhooks and their logs show receiver URLs and full post payloads
